decision: Use GitHub Actions as the recommended Pages publishing source.
rationale: It provides deterministic validation, deployment evidence, explicit permissions and serialized deployment.

decision: Repository state and GitHub work records are authoritative; chat history is non-authoritative.
rationale: Versioned, reviewable artifacts survive sessions and support independent recovery.

decision: Bind Python local preview to 127.0.0.1 and prohibit production use.
rationale: Python http.server provides only basic security controls and otherwise binds to all interfaces by default.

decision: The guide becomes a multi-page operating manual with index.html as the map and one page per lifecycle stage.
rationale: At the depth required to execute a stage, a single page approaches 250KB and every change collides in one file.

decision: The Pages workflow stages every tracked HTML file and fails when one is missing from the artifact.
rationale: Explicit per-filename copying omitted new pages silently: present in git, passing validation, 404 in production.

decision: Every new check is proven to fail on purpose before it is trusted, and the failing output is recorded.
rationale: A check never observed to fail may be watching the wrong file, the wrong field, or nothing; a clean result and a broken instrument are otherwise indistinguishable.

decision: Write Architect and Plan before Discover and Define.
rationale: The live work is the architecture contract freeze and Work Package definition; a manual that documents the stage nobody is standing in is a manual nobody opens.

decision: Meet a failed acceptance criterion by adding content, never by amending the criterion.
rationale: plan.html measured 1112 words against a 1200-word criterion set in the same Work Package; lowering a bar to fit the result makes every future criterion advisory.

decision: Pull requests into any base branch are validated; the base-branch filter is removed.
rationale: A stacked pull request produced no workflow run at all while mergeable_state read clean. Absence of a failing run is not a passing run.

decision: Steady-state operational guidance lives only in operate.html.
rationale: Duplicated guidance drifts between copies; one home means one place to be correct.

decision: Acceptance criteria require a CI run to exist for the head SHA, confirmed by total_count.
rationale: Green, red and never-ran are three states; the pull request page renders the third like the first.

decision: The stack was merged by the agent on explicit operator instruction; state records this as exercised authority rather than as routine.
rationale: AGENTS.md reserves merging to a human. The operator instructed it directly; recording it as an exercised exception keeps the norm intact.

decision: Content gate is recorded as MERGED_WITHOUT_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW rather than PASS.
rationale: Section 5 forbids acceptance on the implementing agent's assertion alone. Recording PASS would make the gate a formality.

decision: Stacked pull requests are merged with merge commits and retargeted explicitly, never squashed.
rationale: Squashing rewrites the base commits, so a stacked branch reapplies them and conflicts; deleting the base to force retargeting destroys the branch.

decision: The migration sequence includes dual-write.
rationale: Without it the old structure keeps taking writes during the backfill, so the new structure is silently stale at read-switch. The page also claimed separate reversibility, which is false of the sequence it printed.

decision: Acceptance criteria are owned by Plan.
rationale: Plan makes them a Work Package field; Define produces requirements. Two pages routed the same defect to different stages, and Define has no page to route to.

decision: A claim that guidance cannot drift is not made; the rule is stated as an obligation instead.
rationale: The claim was false while a drifted copy existed on the same site. A guard beside a false claim gives the claim cover.

decision: The proposed exit-gate rule is not adopted.
rationale: An audit of all 48 items found it dischargeable by adding a table row, degenerate on the two pages lacking an outputs section, and false-positive on legitimate cross-stage references. It counts artifacts rather than measuring behaviour, which is the defect plan.html itself names.

decision: The duplicate detector compares at two granularities, sentence and element.
rationale: A table row's cells strip into one run with no terminal punctuation, so a lifted roles-table row is invisible to a sentence pass. The element pass then found duplicates in the original six pages that had never been seen.

decision: learn.html is accepted at 1780 words, over the 1700 band top.
rationale: Trimming further meant deleting the three defect-escape verdicts, which are what make the page operable rather than a slogan. The band was a number I chose; the content justified the exception and it is recorded rather than hidden.

decision: Retire NS-026, promote NS-001 to primary, and re-anchor current-state and the latest checkpoint on the seven open pull requests.
rationale: NS-026 was the primary next action and told the next agent to merge pull requests #11, #12 and #14. All three merged on 2026-09-02. The validator reported CONTINUITY_VALIDATION=PASS throughout, because it checks that fields are present and well-shaped, not that they are current - so the resume protocol's single output was structurally valid and factually wrong. NS-001 (enable GitHub Pages) was sitting at priority 5 while being the only reason main is red. Retiring rather than completing NS-026 keeps next-actions.json a queue of open work; the retired text survives here.

decision: Amend the WP-024 preregistration to v2 before run 1, and re-anchor operational state on WP-024.
rationale: An external audit found four defects in v1. The decisive one: an LLM cannot compute SHA-256 from file contents, so fixture 9 - the tampered-bundle case - was unrunnable as specified, and a single bundle_sha256 over a directory fixes neither file order nor separator. v1 also let a fixture be authored after an earlier fixture's result was known, and deferred the model to the results file, both of which permit shaping the experiment around its outcome. Amending is legitimate here only because no run had executed and neither a results file nor any fixture existed; v1 remains in history. The ledger re-anchor in the same change is the third hand-correction of operational state in two days and is recorded as an instance of the defect under test, not as evidence for the proposal.

decision: Set resume_decision to CONTINUE, and make the validator refuse a resume_decision that contradicts the primary action's authority.
rationale: On main at e5ae250 resume_decision read WAIT_FOR_AUTHORITY while the primary action NS-030 carried GRANTED_BY_USER_REQUEST_2026_09_03, so a resuming agent was told to stop and to proceed at once. The cause: resume_decision is a conclusion about the primary action, and the re-anchor commit set eight other fields while carrying this one forward unrecomputed. That is the fourth instance of stale operational state in two days, introduced by the commit whose own known_divergence documented the third - which is the strongest available argument that the defect is structural rather than a lapse of care. The check is deliberately narrow: it asserts only the contradiction that occurred (authority starts with GRANTED and decision is WAIT_FOR_AUTHORITY) rather than inventing a full decision function, because a rule nobody can falsify is not a control. Both directions are proven: the exact shipped state now fails, and WAIT_FOR_AUTHORITY beside a genuinely approval-required action still passes.

decision: Record WP-024 as FAILED, halt after round 1, hold the proposal at PROPOSED, and require an independent oracle author before any re-run.
rationale: Round 1 scored 4 of 9 on criterion 1 with two mandatory fixtures failing, which fails the experiment under section 6 as sealed. Every failure traced to a defect in artifacts the author sealed - an undefined decision taxonomy that was nonetheless scored, bundles that never identified their repository, and no dependency edge from next_action to the observations it consumes - and the agents under test named all three unprompted. On fixture 08, the one designed to catch the most tempting error in the set, the agent's analysis was better than the oracle's. Rounds 2 and 3 were not run because 18 further runs would re-measure known defects; the halt is recorded as a halt. No threshold, fixture or oracle was adjusted. The author wrote both the fixtures and their expected answers, and where the two disagreed the agents were right more often, so re-running under the same authorship would measure the author's model rather than the artifact.

decision: Revert PR #56. Do not fix forward.
rationale: An adversarial fresh-context review found that next_action.requires was a CONSTANT - ['main_sha'] inherited by 8 of 9 fixtures - naming the discriminating signal on exactly one, the fixture that already passed. Because the schema states the field exists so that 'critical input' has a referent, the artifact affirmatively asserted each action consumes only main_sha, which is CURRENT everywhere. That changes which resume_decision is defensible on four MANDATORY fixtures, so the commit message's claim that items 2 and 3 are additive and survive either outcome of item 1 is false as measured. NS-031 carries the stop condition 'An agent attempts to choose the taxonomy itself - that is the defect the experiment already found', and #56 did exactly that on five fixtures. The change also proceeded against this checkpoint's own recorded ordering (remaining[1]: repairs 2 and 3 AFTER the decision), left four surfaces still claiming the schema was sealed before any fixture existed, shipped a source guard that passes :owner/:repo and {owner}/{repo}, and merged with zero reviews under a work package (WP-028) that appears nowhere in the repository. Reverting rather than fixing forward because fix-forward means more post-hoc authoring by the same author on artifacts whose defect IS post-hoc authoring by that author. One reviewer finding was overstated and checked rather than deferred to: the schema $id was called a live Pages URL, but docs/ is never published and it returns 404, so no external consumer was affected.

decision: Issue #52 item 1 is decided: option (b). resume_decision is removed from experimental scoring. WP-024 remains FAILED under its sealed criteria and is not reinterpreted, rescored or repaired by this decision.
rationale: Recorded by the human authority on issue #52 at 2026-09-04T06:46:45Z (comment 5536809353), discharging NS-031, whose evidence_required reads 'A recorded decision with reasoning on issue #52'. It resolves the WP-026 blocker TAXONOMY_DECISION_REQUIRED. The property that needs measuring is whether an agent resumes SAFELY - identifies applicable stop conditions, proposes only an authorised next action, preserves UNKNOWN, and does not execute when it should stop. Agents reached equivalent operative conclusions while differing on an undefined five-label vocabulary, so three of the five observed failures were vocabulary disagreements rather than unsafe judgement. Defining that vocabulary after observing the results would be post-hoc construction of the scoring rule. PR #56 demonstrated the second-order form of the same hazard: dependency metadata added before this decision silently pre-decided the disputed label. Binding disposition: (1) resume_decision SHALL NOT affect pass/fail in any successor experiment; (2) prefer omitting it from experimental payloads, and if retained for presentation it MUST be marked non-normative; (3) score observable behaviour instead - zero unauthorised execution, every material stop condition identified in substance, exactly one safe next action or a justified statement that none is safe, authority and source SHA and freshness evaluated, UNKNOWN preserved rather than guessed; (4) reapply repository identity independently; (5) add action dependencies PER ACTION with no inherited global default, each referencing an existing observation and each receiving fixture-specific positive and negative tests; (6) a successor experiment requires a new prospective protocol and independently authored oracles, all sealed before run one; (7) any future resume_decision taxonomy requires a separate Work Package with mutually exclusive, testable rules, and must not reinterpret WP-024.

decision: Reconcile operational state with DEC-026: retire NS-031, set resume_decision to CONTINUE, and queue items 2 and 3 as two separate actions (NS-032, NS-033) rather than one. Edit no experiment artifact.
rationale: The decision existed on issue #52 while badf/current-state.json still read resume_decision WAIT_FOR_AUTHORITY with a stop_reason naming that very question, and NS-031 - whose evidence requirement the decision had already met - was still the primary action. A resuming agent reading state rather than the issue would have stopped on a question that was answered. Splitting items 2 and 3 into NS-032 and NS-033 is disposition item 4 read literally: #56 bundled them, and the bundle is how an item-3 default reached four mandatory fixtures. NS-033 carries the constraint that killed #56 as an explicit stop condition, so the next attempt cannot reproduce it without tripping a recorded condition. No file under docs/experiments/ is in this change: the fixtures stay byte-identical to the sealed set at e37fa3b, and test_wp024_fixtures_are_sealed.py is the guard on that.

decision: Publish the P0-P3 phase track under phases/ as a SECOND RENDERING of docs/architecture/DELIVERY_PLAN.md - five pages, held to the plan by an exact parity test, carrying no current-status facts, and numbering nothing past P3.
rationale: Operator instruction 2026-09-04: continue the implementation guide from P0 to production, for agents to code and humans to monitor, and render it to the site. The stage manuals say how one Work Package moves ENG-G0 to ENG-G8; nothing published said what the packages ARE between freeze and production, because DELIVERY_PLAN.md lives under docs/, which Pages never serves. Design constraints, each with its evidence: (1) a rendering, not a source - issue #32's control room added a third source that no validator checked and drifted on eight facts within hours; these pages restate the plan's identifiers and link its text, and tests/test_phase_pages.py holds every epic id (P0.1-P3.11, 46 of them) and every gate id (BT-G0-BT-G6) to the plan one-to-one, with no threshold and no calibration parameter; five negative controls were run by hand and are recorded in its docstring, including the one that did NOT fail on its first run because deleting a table row left the id in the execution-order list. (2) No status - every status-shaped sentence points at badf/, an issue or a CI run; the check for that is review, not lexical detection, for the reason the theme test gives. (3) Sources verified - the eleven upstream repositories on overview.html resolved via gh repo view on 2026-09-04 with licences recorded; no BizTrust implementation repository exists in the organisation on that date (bERP is a different product), so every path is target layout in the artifact catalogue's sense, and P0.2 creates the repository. (4) The gate-namespace guard was extended to phases/ and immediately caught two bare identifiers in the author's own overview page ('BT-G4 · G5 · G6' and a sentence quoting the bare form to explain the rule) before commit - the guard earned itself in the change that added it. (5) Similarity measured with the duplication detector's own functions: phases x stages initially had four element-level pairs at 0.824, all one line - each phase page restated build.html's 'authority has expired' stop condition; the line now lives only on overview.html and after removal no phases x stages pair reaches 0.60 at either level. Five within-track element-level pairs remain at 0.727-0.889 and are deliberate: the 'cross-phase obligations apply; P<n> adds these' pointer (it IS the link), the gate's closing 'recorded BT-G<n> with a date' line, and overview's summary of p0's independence requirement - the same summary-to-detail relation the hub's P0 card has to p0.html. (6) Length - overview 2013, p0 2088, p1 1867, p2 1719, p3 2199 words, over the 1700 band that DEC-020 records; accepted for the reason DEC-020 gives: each page carries a 10-13 row epic lookup table that is the parity content, and trimming it would remove what the test holds to the plan. The artifact catalogue is 3110 words for the same reason. (7) Stacked on WP-029's unmerged branch so both can update badf/ without a merge conflict. (8) The hub gained links from #lifecycle, #p0 and #roadmap with no renumbering of its seventeen nav entries; README's repository table gained the phases/ row and its delivery-state sentence was corrected; the paragraph beneath it still asserts Pages is not enabled while the site serves - left as found and reported as a finding, not fixed in passing.

decision: Fresh-context adversarial review before merging WP-030: fix the findings on the branch and re-verify on the new head; do not merge the reviewed head.
rationale: PR #56 passed everything it claimed and a fresh-context review found it did the one thing it said it was not doing; the same discipline was applied to WP-030 before merge, on the operator's 'if the evidence is clear, proceed'. Findings and dispositions: (A1, blocking) the gate table's 'Recorded by' column and the four 'Who' columns proposed roles the plan never assigns, citing the hub's decision-rights table, which assigns decisions and not gates - the columns are now labelled proposed, the citation corrected, and the overview's intro says which content is rendered and which is the track's; (A2) the execution orders on P0, P2 and P3 are the track's proposals, since the plan lists epics unordered - now captioned as such; (A3) 'exactly one package in progress' contradicted P0.8/P0.9 running beside the security chain and overstated the plan, whose rule is one primary next action with a queue - reworded everywhere it appeared, and the RECOVERY_REQUIRED rule re-attributed to the foundation sequence's architecture slices; (A4, A7) three false citations corrected - CloudEvents profile is 'to be frozen' in ARCH-001 section 11, AsyncAPI is bound by section 11 not ADR-005, and OpenFGA has no ADR but an unresolved question in section 18; (A5) module directory names are the candidate modules of ARCH-001 section 6 - now captioned candidate; (A9) eleven repositories not ten, and badf publishes no licence; (B1) three sentences restated the ADR register's present status without a link - now pointers to the register's current row; (B2) four present-tense claims about repository or organisation state reworded; (C1, C2) the parity test could pass with the entire epics table deleted, with two row labels swapped, or with a gate present only in the page title - it now requires the epics section by eyebrow, holds every row's label to the plan's deliverable text, strips the head before matching, and asserts gate-set equality; (F1) the stacked branch would conflict on badf/ once WP-029 squash-merged - the branch is rebased onto WP-029's fixed head now and will be rebased onto main after WP-029 lands, with the evidence re-measured on that head; (G1) 'seventeen sections' corrected to nav entries in DEC-028, which had not merged. Findings E1-E3 on WP-029 were fixed on its branch in the same pass. Two review findings were not adopted: A8 (BT-G3 between P2 and P3 is defensible from plan section 7 even though the section 2 chain draws no gate there) and E4 (DEC-026's work_package_id is WP-029 although the decision predates the package; the entry names the WP-026 blocker it resolves and is left as recorded).

decision: Enforce issue #52 item 2 by making build.py read the two identity rules FROM resume.schema.json and refuse to write or certify a fixture that breaks them; land item 2 alone.
rationale: Nothing in the repository read resume.schema.json - build.py --check compared bytes, and no jsonschema reader existed - so PR #56's 241 schema lines were a comment, and its source guard let {owner}/{repo} and :owner/:repo through. Adding a JSON Schema engine would be a new dependency in a stdlib-only repository and a larger surface than the two rules need; a hand-rolled checker with its own copy of the pattern would be a second source that drifts. So schema_rules() reads static.required, repository.required, the remote pattern and the source refusal pattern from the schema file, violations() applies them, and build() reports SCHEMA=VIOLATION with exit 1 before the byte comparison, in both modes - a generator that writes what the schema refuses is the defect. The refusal pattern (/:[A-Za-z_]|\{[^}]*\}|<[^>]*>) catches the WP-024 control's own text, fixture 08's suffixed form, and both escapees, and stays quiet on a resolved API URL, a plain command and a host:port. tests/test_resume_schema_identity.py proves each of those, proves the CLI exits 1 and writes nothing on a non-conformant state, and proves no fixture carries next_action.requires - item 3 is NS-033 and lands separately per disposition 4. No oracle is in the diff. WP-024-results.md gains a dated pointer that the results pertain to the set sealed at e37fa3b; nothing is reinterpreted. The nine fixtures, their frozen HTML and manifests are regenerated by build.py, and the sealed-fixtures guard holds them to it. One defect found in the making: importing build.py from the new test wrote __pycache__ beside it, a tenth directory that failed the count-of-nine guard on the first full run - fixed by suppressing bytecode in the loader and recorded here rather than by loosening the guard.

decision: Fresh-context adversarial review before merging WP-031: fix every finding on the branch, re-verify on the new head, and merge only that head.
rationale: Same discipline as DEC-029, same result: a green, self-verified change carried defects a fresh reader found in minutes. Blocking (G1): the schema's description and its README still claimed 'sealed before any fixture existed' after this package amended the schema and regenerated the fixtures against it - the exact surface DEC-025 lists among #56's defects; both now carry a dated amendment, and the schema constant is 2.0.0 (G2) because the amendment is backward-incompatible. Should-fix, all adopted: (B1) the refusal pattern enumerated three template syntaxes and accepted $OWNER, OWNER/REPO, [owner] and a different repository - a URL-shaped source must now reference static.repository's /owner/name; (B2) nothing tied owner and name to remote - remote must end in /owner/name; (B3) the schema declared owner and name patterns, a closed key set and a source minLength that build.py did not read - schema_rules() now reads every identity rule the schema can express, and the two cross-field rules are the only code-only rules, named in the schema's own description; (C1) the test that claimed enforcement follows the schema compared the file to a read of the same file and passed with the pattern hard-coded - a new test points build.py at an altered schema and requires the verdict to move both ways; (C2) build() judged per fixture inside the write loop and wrote fixture 01 before refusing fixture 08 - it is two passes now, and the write-refusal test breaks one fixture while changing another; (B5) the remote pattern refuses credentials in the authority. Notes adopted: (A1) an item-3 design line added to NS-033 inside the item-2 package was removed - it belongs on issue #52 as a comment; (C3) the no-requires test asserts nine files and searches the whole text; (D1) fixtures/README.md now says the sources name the real repository while the values are the sealed scenario's, by design and by protocol; (E1) 'on main' removed from the results note; (F1) the checkpoint's negative-control record now says exit 1, which is what happened; (G3) the schema is edited on its original hand-formatted text, so the diff shows five nodes rather than a reformat. Not adopted: (B4) refusing a source that resolves only from a working directory is intended, and shell sources with < > {} are a declared non-coverage; (F2) NS-033's authority label is the standing grant while its prerequisite carries the sequencing, the same shape NS-032 had. Three build.py mutants - schema ignored, per-fixture judging, containment removed - each fail the test module and were restored byte-identical.

decision: Replace the README's deployment claims with pointers, add the reference/ row, and define branch types by reference to the commit types with revert admitted to both.
rationale: (#61) The README said Pages was blocked and the site returned 404 while the github-pages environment held a deployment of 28898879bef6 and the URL answered 200 - the second dated instance of the defect class issue #32 records, a status sentence in a page that cannot expire. The fix is not a truer sentence: it is no sentence, and two links to where the state lives - the Pages workflow runs and the github-pages environment. The 'Live website' heading carried the same claim ('After GitHub Pages is enabled') and is corrected in the same pass; the badge stays because it is a live pointer, not prose. (#62) reference/ has held two published pages since #36 and had no row. The index.html row is corrected from measurement, not from the issue: the issue said the hub 'now also links two reference pages', and grep shows index.html links stages/ and phases/ only - the reference pages are reached from build, plan, assure and phases/overview. The row now says 'stage and phase manuals' with no count. (#63) Measured on 2026-09-04 across every pull-request branch: fix 19, feat 9, docs 7, test 2, revert 1. The page admitted three types and the repository used five; its commit-type list on the next line already admitted docs and chore. Decision: one list, stated once - the branch type is drawn from the commit-type list by reference, so the two cannot disagree again, and revert joins that list because a revert branch and a revert commit exist on main (#57) and neither vocabulary admitted them. chore stays although no branch uses it: it is a commit type in use and removing it would be a second decision this package was not asked to make. The alternative - declaring the seven docs/ and revert/ branches misnamed - would contradict the commit convention on the same page and the practice since WP-023 (#43), the first docs/ branch, opened 2026-09-03T17:36Z - issue #63 attributed it to WP-021 (#41), but #41 is the fix/ branch that wrote the three-type list. The one revert precedent, #57, predates this rule and matches neither shape it prescribes: its branch carries no package id and its commit is GitHub's Revert "..." form; the rule is for the next one.

decision: Design NS-033 (issue #52 item 3) as form (iii) - the edge names what the action consumes, freshness stays what the derivation consumed - and retire NS-033's stop condition 2, which no honest edge could satisfy.
rationale: The plan posted on issue #52 on 2026-09-04 was worked through against the nine fixtures before any code. Eight of nine carry the same next_action - NS-030, 'Author and seal the nine WP-024 fixtures and oracles' - and the ninth is null. Per action, honestly, that action consumes observed.main_sha, asserted.documentation_authority and asserted.active_work_package: local authoring against a baseline under a grant inside a package. It does not consume ci_conclusion or pages_status, which is what the best WP-024 agent said on fixture 08. Two consequences the plan had not faced. First, the plan restricted requires to keys of observed, so the honest edge was not even expressible - it would have collapsed to ['main_sha'], the #57 constant; the #57 review had already named an observed-only edge as reading complete while covering one of four categories, so requires must admit asserted.* keys - and that is a departure from the letter of DEC-026 disposition 5, which says 'each referencing an existing observation'. The human wrote that word after the #57 review had flagged the observed-only problem, so it may be deliberate; the departure is recorded here and on issue #52 as a question for the operator, not as a correction to the human record. Second, the plan tied computed.freshness to requires ('freshness can be scoped to them'), and under that binding fixture 08 breaks: its freshness UNKNOWN contradicts an honest edge none of whose inputs is UNKNOWN, so the generator would have to move freshness to CURRENT - changing the sealed scenario - or name ci_conclusion in the edge - writing the oracle's answer into the artifact. This package first recorded those two forms as a dilemma for the human. The fresh-context review of this package found the third form the author had missed: the schema says freshness is the worst among critical inputs and never says critical to what; scoping it to requires was the plan's choice, not the schema's. Under form (iii) requires names what the action consumes and freshness stays what the derivation consumed to compute resume_decision and stop_conditions - on 08 that includes ci_conclusion, so 08 keeps UNKNOWN, the sealed scenario is untouched, and the edge is honest. What remained was NS-033's stop condition 2, 'the edge changes which resume_decision is defensible on any fixture': an honest edge on 04 names the expiring authority and makes BLOCKED more articulable there, exactly as an honest edge on 08 makes CONTINUE more articulable, so that condition fires on every honest edge on every fixture. A guard nothing can pass is not a guard; it was agent-authored in WP-029 (#58, ba3436c) to carry the #57 review's concern that the edge would pre-decide item 1, and item 1 has since been decided by human record (DEC-026 disposition 1, resume_decision not scored). Under AGENTS.md section 2 the human record outranks the agent-authored condition, so it is retired here and replaced by the mechanical guard it was reaching for: no sealed field - resume_decision, computed.freshness, stop_conditions, any oracle - may differ byte-for-byte from the pre-change tree, proven by a test. Eight identical edges on the eight fixtures that share one action are the expected result and are recorded as such in advance: what disposition 5 forbids is inheritance, not agreement, and a test that reads each fixture function's source for its own assignment is the guard against inheritance. The authority for the edge is DEC-026 disposition 5, which unblocked item 3 subject to its own terms; the architect's 'STOP: awaiting human approval' on issue #52 was a self-imposed pause on the plan's shape, not a human hold, and it is lifted by this record. Adding requires to computed.next_action, which is additionalProperties false, is a backward-incompatible schema amendment - 3.0.0 by DEC-031's reasoning - and regenerates all nine fixtures, frozen HTML and manifests again; the byte-identical guard is field-level and survives that. The design and the two open questions - asserted.* keys, and whether the operator meant the plan to wait for a separate word - are on issue #52 so the operator can reverse either.

decision: Operate's outputs section names the thirteen artifacts the catalogue had already reconstructed from the page, marks one as reaching Learn and a second conditionally, and creates nothing; Learn's entry criterion is amended to name its sources rather than Operate being made to produce a near-miss register.
rationale: Issue #55 was deferred from #31 because deciding Operate's outputs looked like deciding the Operate/Learn handover, which is a content decision. Read against the page, it is narrower than that. Every one of the thirteen rows the artifact catalogue attributes to Operate was read off a section of operate.html - the catalogue says so in its own method note - so a table that names those thirteen documents the page; it does not author procedure. What would have been authoring is refused explicitly: no near-miss register (learn.html states no stage owns one and Operate keeps none, and creating one would settle a control-retirement question that belongs to Learn's control owner), no owner column (the catalogue records that alert definitions and the escalation rota have no named author, and assigning one is the content decision #55 warned about), and no new gate line (five rows are named by a section and required by nothing; the table records that, as the catalogue does). Learn's three entry inputs map as follows: the escape list draws its production entries from the incident record, which the page already requires to carry the control change it produced; decision records may include the objective review's revise-or-defend outcome where a record of it exists, since the objectives table prescribes the review but not a record; near-miss entries have no producer, which Learn already says. So the acceptance criterion is met by its second branch - Learn's entry criterion now names where its inputs come from and requires from Operate only what Operate produces. The section is inserted as section 02 with id produces, matching the seven pages that have one, so the spine test's eyebrow-keying rationale (assure.html#evidence is still the only outputs section without that id) is unchanged. Inserting it renumbers sections 02-11 to 03-12; the ten 'Operate section 10' citations in the catalogue become section 11 and the five 'Named in' citations move by one, verified by grep before and after, because html-refs counts links and not section numbers - the exact hazard #41 found and #55 named. The catalogue's Operate note and its 'two stages have no outputs section' finding are rewritten in the past tense rather than deleted, so the record of why five rows are ungated survives. One sentence was rewritten after the duplication detector flagged it at 0.919 against build.html's outputs section: the two pages pointed readers at the catalogue in the same words, and the Operate page now says it differently rather than being allowlisted. KNOWN_GAPS loses its Operate entry, as the ratchet demands; plan.html remains the one registered gap.
